scenes.heading: gRPC & Protocol Buffers
scenes.narration: Let's explore gRPC and Protocol Buffers, the de-facto standard for how Go microservices talk to each other.

scenes.heading: From .proto to a live call
steps: Define messages and a service in a .proto
Generate typed Go client and server code
Call over a multiplexed HTTP/2 stream
scenes.narration: gRPC is contract-first. You define your messages and service once in a proto file, then protoc generates strongly-typed Go structs plus a client and server interface. You implement the server interface with your business logic, the client dials a single long-lived connection, and each call is marshaled to compact binary and sent over an HTTP slash two stream. That one connection multiplexes many concurrent calls.

scenes.heading: Why it beats hand-rolled JSON
items: Fields keyed by number, so schemas evolve safely
Four RPC shapes including native streaming
scenes.narration: The wire format keys every field by its number, not its name, which is why you can rename freely but must never reuse a number — that rule is the basis of safe schema evolution. gRPC supports four RPC shapes, from simple unary to bidirectional streaming, all riding one HTTP slash two connection. That multiplexing and the compact binary encoding make it far leaner than opening a fresh connection per JSON request.

scenes.heading: Implementing the generated server
scenes.narration: Here we implement the generated GetUser method. The crucial detail is the error: instead of returning a plain Go error, we return status dot Errorf with codes dot NotFound. That structured status code travels across the wire, so the client can inspect it and render a proper 404. A plain error would be flattened to codes dot Unknown, losing all its meaning.

scenes.text: Reuse one *grpc.ClientConn, always set a context deadline, and use interceptors for logging, auth, and recovery.
scenes.narration: In production, reuse a single client connection because HTTP slash two multiplexes over it, always set a context deadline so calls can't hang, and centralize logging, auth, tracing, and panic recovery in interceptors — gRPC's equivalent of HTTP middleware.
